chapter: The jazz war with Leonard Feather
title: The Lester Young record date that Feather's article killed
summary: A Harlem label wanted blues with Lester Young and Hodes, but cancelled after Feather's Metronome piece. Hodes will put the article in his book.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: You said that he cost you a record date.

That cost me a record date. Well, Harlem recording outfit, where there was -- I can't remember the title, got very interested in doing blues with Lester Young and Art Hodes. Only they told me over the phone, don't do no sadass blues. Do blues that are -- got some brightness and yet feeling, but let it jump a little.

So that we could sell. We had it set up. I had no paper, but I had his word and I had all these conversations. And when he read that article, he called me up the next day and says, I'm sorry, I can't go through it.
What article was that? -in Down Beat-
Leonard wrote in Metronome that he could play me under the table, that I was -- oh, it was a terrible writeup. We have it, by the way. We have a copy of it, and

it'll go in the book. To show-- and I probably won't write the chapter, I'll just write the chapter I related about this incident that happened between my friend and things like that. But Chet, who is an educator and an English prof at the Circle [University of Chicago] campus will look up all the material which he now has and put it down as a --
